name: Zacatepec Eastern Chatino, ZAC
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Villard, Stéphanie. 2015. The Phonology and Morphology of Zacatepec Eastern Chatino. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Austin. xxii+450 pp. (hdl 2152/31492; open UT repository PDF, archived copy (Internet Archive, 2022))
catalog_quote: nasalization and vowel length only occur underlyingly in a very restricted domain, i.e the (final) prominent syllable[2] ... [fn.2] The prominence is based on the level of contrastiveness. The final syllable is the most prominent syllable in ZAC because this is where the most contrast occurs at the segmental level as well as at the prosodic level. (p.49) || Table 3.2 shows the distribution of phonemes according to manner of articulation within the word. It clearly shows how the final syllable is the most prominent, as it is the position in the Word where the most contrast occurs. (p.138) || In the tonal analysis presented in this work, the mora is also the minimal Tone Bearing Unit (henceforth TBU). (p.40) || Tones link to the prominent mora (the final mora) in the stem, from right to left, in a one to one fashion. When there are more tones than moras to be linked to a word, all left over tones are left unrealized. When there are more moras than tones, any left-over moras are unspecified for tone. Floating tones are always preserved. There can only be a maximum of 3 linked tones per word. (fig. 4.23, p.199)
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (472-page PDF with text, XeTeX 2015; extracted text page extraction). All three quoted passages are present verbatim at the stated locators: (1) p.71 = printed p.49, sec. 2.2 'Vocalic system': 'nasalization and vowel length only occur underlyingly in a very restricted domain, i.e the (final) prominent syllable[2]' with fn.2 'The prominence is based on the level of contrastiveness. The final syllable is the most prominent syllable in ZAC because this is where the most contrast occurs at the segmental level as well as at the prosodic level.'; (2) p.160 = printed p.138, sec. 3.2 'Phoneme distribution within the word': 'It clearly shows how the final syllable is the most prominent…
new_statements.rule_in_words: ZAC is a tone language (lexical tonal sequences linked to moras); the word-final syllable of the simplex word is the prominent syllable: it alone hosts contrastive vowel length, nasal vowels and the full vowel/consonant inventory, and tones associate starting from its final mora. The author grounds 'prominence' in contrast licensing and does not use the term 'stress' for native vocabulary.
new_statements.exceptions: Only fn.8 p.69: some Spanish loans with penultimate stress keep a lengthened penultimate vowel (e.g. rrumèyō 'medicine' [r̥ume:jo]), described as loan accommodation, not a phonological rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the simplex (non-compound) phonological word ω minus enclitics; prominence = final syllable of ω. Statement is distributional/phonological, not an acoustic stress claim; no phrase-level stress discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes the Chatino of San Marcos Zacatepec, Oaxaca (ZAC), i.e. exactly Glottolog zaca1242 / ISO ctz; data mainly from elderly speakers (language moribund). No dialect mismatch.

new_statements.citation: Woodbury, Anthony C. 2019. Conjugational double-classing: The separate life cycles of prefix classes vs tone ablaut classes in aspect/mood inflection in the Chatino languages of Oaxaca. Amerindia 41: 75-120.
new_statements.check: reported on verification, not yet confirmed
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one listed work (Woodbury 2019), so the two-work spot-check floor could not be met from the works list; that one work was searched in full (see evidence) and is confirmed silent. As a substitute I a full-text search for stress/accent the two other files already saved in the zaca1242 folder by the earlier reading (not listed works, not added): Villard 2008 CILLA-III (Spanish) has no stress/acento term; its 'penúltima sílaba' lines (pp. 1-2) are about ZAC retaining the penultimate syllable of roots, not stress. Cruz & Woodbury 2014 LD&C 8, Table 5, p. 500, reproduces the 2006 ZAC transcription with 'su4ká2 sugar, chi4lyó2 knife (´marks strong stress)' -- a stress mark on Spanish loans on…

tone_statements.citation: Woodbury, Anthony C. 2014. The exuberant tonal system of San Marcos Zacatepec Eastern Chatino. Paper presented to the Surrey Morphology Group, University of Surrey, Guildford, UK, 12 March 2014 (slides; based on joint work with Stephanie Villard). Deposited 2018 in the Chatino Language Documentation dataverse, Texas Data Repository. doi:10.18738/T8/BGPA1O (CC0).
tone_statements.quote: How it is “exuberant”? Phonetically and phonologically: Five tones (L(ow), M(id), H(igh), LH, LS(uperhigh)) Tones link to moras Moras may also be toneless High (& superhigh)-ending tones persist (or “spread”) into toneless moras to the end of the utterance Some words carry one of three floating tones ((L), (H), (LS)); Floating tones link to the rightmost toneless mora in the next word, if any ... Really five tones? Historical considerations ... I say yes, synchronically, because the tones are invariant—they participate in no alternations (faithfulness)
tone_statements.locator: slide 2 'How it is “exuberant”?' and slide 58 'Really five tones?'
tone_statements.summary: 5 tones (3 level, 2 rising) on moras; toneless moras default to low falling; 3 floating tones; 15 stem tone-sequence classes; downstep not discussed (slight declination only); tables are images.

tone_statements.citation: Villard, Stephanie. 2012. La tonologia verbal en el chatino oriental de Zacatepec. Handout, XII Encuentro Internacional de Linguistica en el Noroeste, Universidad de Sonora, Hermosillo, 15 November 2012. Deposited 2018, Texas Data Repository, doi:10.18738/T8/ZHBD9I (CC0).
tone_statements.quote: Hay CINCO ELEMENTOS TONALES los cuales son asociados a moras o son transportados (flotan) a las secuencias de moras no asociadas (sin tono) en la palabra posterior. Una mora puede ocurrir con cualquier elemento tonal o ocurrir sin tono. Una palabra aislada sin tono asociado se pronuncia con un nivel bajo. Tabla 1... B(ajo) à La mora es baja, nivelada ... M(edio) ā ... A(lto) á ... Ascendente (R) ǎ La mora ascende del nivel bajo al nivel medio-alto ... Ascendente super alto (R^) ả La mora ascende del nivel bajo al nivel super-alto ... Existen 14 CLASES LEXICALES TONALES
tone_statements.translation: There are FIVE TONAL ELEMENTS, which are associated to moras or are carried (float) onto sequences of unassociated (toneless) moras in the following word. A mora may occur with any tonal element or occur without tone. An isolated word with no associated tone is pronounced at a low level. Table 1... L(ow) à the mora is low, level ... M(id) ā ... H(igh) á ... Rising (R) ǎ the mora rises from low to mid-high level ... Super-high rising (R^) ả the mora rises from low to super-high level ... There are 14 LEXICAL TONE CLASSES
tone_statements.locator: p. 3 sec. 1.b.i and Tabla 1, plus p. 4 sec. 1.b.ii
tone_statements.summary: 3 level + 2 rising tonal elements linked to moras; toneless moras allowed; floating tones (R-B, R, R^) dock on the next word; 14 lexical tone classes; aspect/person marked by tonal alternation.

tone_statements.quote: (1) Elementos tonales. Hay CINCO ELEMENTOS TONALES los cuales son asociados a moras o son transportados (flotan) a las secuencias de moras no asociadas (sin tono) en la palabra posterior: ... L(ow) [bajo] ... M(id) [medio] ... H(igh) [alto] ... R(ising) [ascendente] ... La mora ascende del nivel bajo a mid-alto ... R^ (ising: super high) [ascendente] super-alto ... La mora ascende del nivel bajo a super-alto ... (2) Las clases lexicales Existen 13 CLASES LEXICALES TONALES , cada una definida por una SECUENCIA DE ELEMENTOS TONALES específica
tone_statements.translation: (1) Tonal elements. There are FIVE TONAL ELEMENTS, which are associated to moras or are carried over (float) onto the sequences of unassociated (toneless) moras in the following word: ... L(ow) ... M(id) ... H(igh) ... R(ising): the mora rises from low to mid-high ... R^ (rising super-high): the mora rises from low to super-high ... (2) Lexical classes. There are 13 LEXICAL TONE CLASSES, each defined by a specific SEQUENCE OF TONAL ELEMENTS
tone_statements.locator: p. 3, sec. 2 'Análisis del sistema tonal de ZAC', (1)-(2)
tone_statements.summary: Five tonal elements (L, M, H level; R, R^ rising) linked right-to-left to moras of the word; 13 lexical tone-sequence classes; floating ]L ]R ]R^ realized on following toneless moras; H/R/R^ spread.

tone_statements.citation: Woodbury, Anthony C. 2012. La diversidad tipologica del tono en los idiomas chatinos. XII Encuentro Internacional de Linguistica en el Noroeste, Hermosillo, Sonora (PowerPoint with wav audio). Deposited 2018, Texas Data Repository, doi:10.18738/T8/IQT2DF.
tone_statements.quote: 4. ZAC: Sistema tonal: los elementos tonales (“tonos”) ... Asociado a la mora ... X (sin tono) a Bajo descendiente (por defecto) B(ajo) à Bajo descendiente M(edio) ā Medio nivel A(lto) á Alto nivel BA ǎ Bajo a alto BA↑ ả Bajo a superalto ... Los 5 tonos occurren en solo 14 secuencias (Tambien, incluyen las secuencias Tonos Flotantes (superescritos) que describimos más abajo) ... Aunque los tonos pertenecen a moras, las secuencias pertenecen a las raíces (o bases)
tone_statements.translation: 4. ZAC: Tonal system: the tonal elements ('tones') ... Associated to the mora ... X (toneless) a low falling (by default); B (low) à low falling; M (mid) ā mid level; A (high) á high level; BA ǎ low to high; BA↑ ả low to superhigh ... The 5 tones occur in only 14 sequences (they also include the Floating Tone sequences (superscript) described below) ... Although the tones belong to moras, the sequences belong to the roots (or bases)
tone_statements.summary: Five tonal elements on the mora (levels B, M, A; contours BA, BA-superhigh) plus toneless moras; only 14 root/base tone sequences, some with floating tones; high tones spread onto toneless syllables.

tone_statements.citation: Campbell, Eric W. & Anthony C. Woodbury. 2010. The comparative tonology of Chatino: A prolegomenon. Handout, Society for the Study of the Indigenous Languages of the Americas Annual Meeting, Baltimore MD, 9 January 2010. Deposited 2018, Chatino Language Documentation dataverse, Texas Data Repository, doi:10.18738/T8/Z4WIUV (CC0); open project copy also at drive.google.com/file/d/1g3_CUZHLH9WkUuJNaDAA-jWAwKTywYCZ.
tone_statements.quote: ZACATEPEC (H. Cruz & Woodbury 2006, Villard 2008) • Domain is the BASE, but the lexical “tones” are sequences of 0, 1 or 2 LINKING ELEMENTS • Floating tones (written ᴴ) • Large tone inventory o Linking elements: X (unmarked; strictly speaking, the absence of a linking element), L, M, H, R(ising), Rº (rise to superhigh), written over vowels (a, à, ā, á, ǎ, ǎº) o Rising combinations: XMᴴ, LMᴴ, MH, XR, LRº o Level combinations: X, XLᴴ, MM o Falling combinations: HM, RL, RºL • Extensive sandhi alternations including the spreading of H and R tones over unmarked (X) mora
tone_statements.locator: p. 3, sec. 3.1 Eastern Chatino, item (6) ZACATEPEC
tone_statements.summary: 11 lexical tone patterns on the base from 6 linking elements (X, L, M, H, R, Rº); superscript H = floating tone. Credits H. Cruz & Woodbury 2006, Villard 2008; aspect prefixes add more combinations.

tone_statements.citation: Cruz, Hilaria & Anthony C. Woodbury. 2006. La fonologia y tonologia comparativa del chatino: un informe de campo en Zacatepec. In Memorias del Congreso de Idiomas Indigenas de Latinoamerica-II (CILLA II), University of Texas at Austin / Archive of the Indigenous Languages of Latin America. Open copy linked from the Chatino Language Documentation Project site (drive.google.com/file/d/1hzjVTibSrIgqcG_6JiNwZuTeHD-aNik6); original AILLA URL www.ailla.utexas.org/site/cilla2/ no longer serves the PDF.
tone_statements.quote: A continuación presentamos el inventario de los tonos de los cuales son nueve: (7) Inventorio de los tonos (1 alto; 4 bajo) 3-4 3-1 41 4-2 4-21 14 4-2’ 3-24 2-4 Estas representaciones consisten primeramente de indicadores de frecuencia fundamental, del “1”, el más alto, al “4” el más bajo. Las sequencias numéricas indican contornos de tonos... Tal como en todas las variedades del Chatino hemos considerado que cada raíz –sean monosilábica or disilábica- llevan un solo tono, y cada tono esta alineado con una sola raíz.
tone_statements.translation: Next we present the inventory of the tones, of which there are nine: (7) Inventory of the tones (1 high; 4 low) 3-4 3-1 41 4-2 4-21 14 4-2' 3-24 2-4. These representations consist first of indicators of fundamental frequency, from '1', the highest, to '4', the lowest. The numeric sequences indicate tone contours... As in all varieties of Chatino we have considered that each root, whether monosyllabic or disyllabic, carries a single tone, and each tone is aligned with a single root.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 3 'Sistema de tonos y su correspondencia', ex. (7) and following paragraphs
tone_statements.summary: Nine root tone melodies on a 4-level scale (1 high, 4 low); authors call the analysis preliminary; one-part tones leave a default 3 on the penult; example count is a floor; F0 wording, no measurement.

States the final syllable is 'the most prominent syllable in ZAC' because it hosts the most segmental and prosodic contrast (fn.2 p.49; sec.3.2 p.138); vowel length and nasality realized only in the final syllable; tones link to 'the prominent mora (the final mora)' right-to-left (fig.4.23 p.199). Only 'stress' mention: fn.8 p.69, Spanish loans with penultimate stress get that vowel lengthened.

sources.citation: Woodbury, Anthony C. 2019. Conjugational double-classing: The separate life cycles of prefix classes vs tone ablaut classes in aspect/mood inflection in the Chatino languages of Oaxaca. Amerindia 41: 75-120.
sources.note: Pan-Chatino overview by the project PI; may contain a one-line family-wide statement that the final syllable is stressed/prominent, covering ZAC.

tone.says: Record/title only: cross-Chatino study of aspect/mood inflection in which verbs fall simultaneously into prefix conjugation classes and largely orthogonal TONE-ABLAUT conjugation classes (grammatical tone alternations depending partly on the stem's lexical tone), with separate diachronic 'life cycles' across the Chatino varieties; whether Tataltepec paradigms (Sullivant 2015) are among the varieties tabulated was not verified in the text.

tone.translation: 4. ZAC: Tonal system: the tonal elements ('tones') ... Associated to the mora ... X (toneless) a low falling (by default); B (low) à low falling; M (mid) ā mid level; A (high) á high level; BA ǎ low to high; BA↑ ả low to superhigh ... The 5 tones occur in only 14 sequences (they also include the Floating Tone sequences (superscript) described below) ... Although the tones belong to moras, the sequences belong to the roots (or bases)

Cruz & Woodbury 2006, Villard 2008) • Domain is the BASE, but the lexical “tones” are sequences of 0, 1 or 2 LINKING ELEMENTS • Floating tones (written ᴴ) • Large tone inventory o Linking elements: X (unmarked; strictly speaking, the absence of a linking element), L, M, H, R(ising), Rº (rise to superhigh), written over vowels (a, à, ā, á, ǎ, ǎº) o Rising combinations: XMᴴ, LMᴴ, MH, XR, LRº o Level combinations: X, XLᴴ, MM o Falling combinations: HM, RL, RºL • Extensive sandhi alternations including the spreading of H and R tones over unmarked (X) mora

sources.quote: A continuación presentamos el inventario de los tonos de los cuales son nueve: (7) Inventorio de los tonos (1 alto; 4 bajo) 3-4 3-1 41 4-2 4-21 14 4-2’ 3-24 2-4 Estas representaciones consisten primeramente de indicadores de frecuencia fundamental, del “1”, el más alto, al “4” el más bajo. Las sequencias numéricas indican contornos de tonos... Tal como en todas las variedades del Chatino hemos considerado que cada raíz –sean monosilábica or disilábica- llevan un solo tono, y cada tono esta alineado con una sola raíz.

tone.quote: A continuación presentamos el inventario de los tonos de los cuales son nueve: (7) Inventorio de los tonos (1 alto; 4 bajo) 3-4 3-1 41 4-2 4-21 14 4-2’ 3-24 2-4 Estas representaciones consisten primeramente de indicadores de frecuencia fundamental, del “1”, el más alto, al “4” el más bajo. Las sequencias numéricas indican contornos de tonos... Tal como en todas las variedades del Chatino hemos considerado que cada raíz –sean monosilábica or disilábica- llevan un solo tono, y cada tono esta alineado con una sola raíz.
tone.locator: sec. 3 'Sistema de tonos y su correspondencia', ex. (7) and following paragraphs
tone.translation: Next we present the inventory of the tones, of which there are nine: (7) Inventory of the tones (1 high; 4 low) 3-4 3-1 41 4-2 4-21 14 4-2' 3-24 2-4. These representations consist first of indicators of fundamental frequency, from '1', the highest, to '4', the lowest. The numeric sequences indicate tone contours... As in all varieties of Chatino we have considered that each root, whether monosyllabic or disyllabic, carries a single tone, and each tone is aligned with a single root.
tone.summary: Nine root tone melodies on a 4-level scale (1 high, 4 low); authors call the analysis preliminary; one-part tones leave a default 3 on the penult; example count is a floor; F0 wording, no measurement.
